newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks tumble to sharply lower close.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks tumble to sharply lower close.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks tumbled to a sharply lower close on Thursday, as stock index futures plummeted and worries remerged about the health of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index slid 222.66 points, or 1.65 percent, to 13,239.95. Turnover was HK$8.71 billion compared with HK$6.84 billion on Wednesday.
February Hang Seng futures fell 300 points to 13,120.
"Rumours about Deng's health surfaced again this afternoon which led the index to drop significantly," said Henry Lui, research analyst at Mansion House Research.
Currency dealers said an afternoon weakening in the Hong Kong dollar against the U.S. dollar coincided with a sudden fall in stocks.
"I think it is really just the current strength of the (U.S.) dollar which is doing it," said Christopher Ward, director at Peregrine Fixed Income, of the Hong Kong dollar's weakness.

Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities, said the stock market's drop was surprising given the strength of Wall Street overnight. The Dow industrials closed at a record high on Wednesday, rising 103.52 points to 6,961.63, prompting an early jump in the Hang Seng Index to a high of 13,589.70 points.
"The market is looking really sick," said Ng.

Lui said the market could come under further selling pressure in the short term but some investors had been reducing their holdings over the last few weeks and may start accumulating blue chips around current levels.
Morgan Stanley regional strategist Peter Churchouse said earlier on Thursday that Hong Kong stocks could face some consolidation over the near term.
He said lingering concerns about politics, the Hong Kong dollar and the property market could unsettle the market.
"On a 12-month view, I am still pretty positive on Hong Kong, although over the next month or two we expect a bit of consolidation," he told Reuters.

Among the major blue chips, Cheung Kong fell HK$2.75 to HK$72.00 and Henderson Land slumped HK$2.00 to HK$69.00. HSBC Holdings dropped HK$1.50 to HK$186.00 and Hang Seng Bank fell HK$1.25 to HK$89.50.
China Light fell HK$0.70 to HK$35.00. It said it would launch a voluntary departure scheme next month in its generation business group.
